title: Pick the equation that fits the scatterplot
subtitle: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots · 18 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **18 of the official questions in Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots are this one** — 10 Easy, 4 Medium, 4 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question asks which equation 'best models', 'could be a line of best fit for', or 'best represents' the data.
- The choices are four equations of the same family, such as y = mx + b, ax^2 + bx + c, or a*b^x, that differ only in signs and the size of the constants.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Identify the shape: straight, U-shaped or upside-down U, or curved toward the axis (exponential).
- 2) Use the sign of the key coefficient: slope sign for a line, leading coefficient for a parabola (negative opens down), and base above or below 1 for exponential growth or decay.
- 3) Use the y-intercept, where the data would meet the y-axis, to choose between the remaining options.
- For a parabola, check the vertex x-value with -b/2a if needed.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Graph each choice with the viewing window set to match the plot's axes and see which curve passes through the middle of the cloud.
Or enter a few estimated points in a table and run a regression, for example y1~ax1^2+bx1+c or y1~ab^x1, then pick the closest choice.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: Two choices share the right shape but have the wrong intercept, or share the intercept but have the wrong sign on the slope or leading coefficient.
For exponential models, you treat a base between 0 and 1 as growth.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
